subject: VAL
label: Grade 12 Science
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 12 Science Values and life skills, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 2 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Leadership and ethics
modules.outcome: lead a team project with an ethical review
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Leadership and ethics', taught in a way that is with exam-style questions and written reasoning. The target is clear: lead a team project with an ethical review. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen and talk: hear a short story, text or example linked to 'Leadership and ethics' and say what it means in your own words.
Connect: name one place in your own day where it applies.
Use it: lead a team project with an ethical review. Practise with care and respect, in class and at home.
Reflect: what went well, what was hard, and one thing you will do next time.
modules.example: Solved: Ethical decision steps: facts, who is affected, options, which value each option meets, choose, review later. Method: Model run for 'Leadership and ethics'. A short text or story is read aloud. Learners say the main lesson in one sentence. In pairs they find one moment in school or home where this lesson would help. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Lead a team project with an ethical review: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
steps: Step 1, The project: Aref leads a team of four on a lab project measuring the time a trolley takes to roll down a ramp. Roles: Aref leads, Dina measures, Hamad records, Sara analyses the data.

Step 2, Ethical rules: Record every trial honestly, do not change data to match a hoped result, give credit for help and report all methods. These rules are agreed and written in the project log before the first trial.
Step 3, The data: Five timing trials in seconds are 12.1, 12.3, 11.9, 12.2 and 14.8. The sum is 63.3, so the mean is 63.3 divided by 5, which is 12.66 seconds. The last result is far from the others.

Step 4, The temptation: Hamad suggests deleting 14.8 without saying so, because it spoils the neat result. Aref asks, 'Would we be comfortable explaining this to our teacher?' The team decides the outlier cannot be silently removed.

Step 5, The honest treatment: They investigate and find that Dina stopped the timer late on trial 5. They report all five values and explain the probable error. Without that trial the mean is 48.5 divided by 4, which is 12.125 seconds.

Step 6, Review the leadership: The report shows both means, 12.66 and 12.125, and states the reason. The team rates itself out of 5: honesty 5, method 4, teamwork 4. Aref notes that one more trial would have helped. Honest reporting makes results trustworthy.

Your turn: Trials 8.0, 8.2, 8.1 and 9.9. What do you report? Model answer: all four values; mean with all is 34.2 divided by 4, which is 8.55; without 9.9 it is 8.1; explain the cause and repeat the trial.

modules.standard: Prepare a study plan, a CV and a statement of purpose: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
steps: Step 1, Study plan: Yousef has 8 weeks before exams and plans 20 hours per week: Mathematics 6, Physics 5, Chemistry 5, Computer Science 4. Check 6 plus 5 plus 5 plus 4 is 20. Over 8 weeks that is 160 hours.

Step 2, Weekly schedule: Maths gets three 2-hour sessions of problem practice; Physics and Chemistry each get one 2-hour session of theory and one 3-hour session of past-style questions; Computer Science gets four 1-hour coding sessions.

Step 3, CV structure: Name and contact, profile, education with subjects, projects, achievements and skills. Example bullet: 'Built a Python program to log lab readings, reducing a 30-minute table task to 5 minutes.' It fits one page.

Step 4, Evidence and honesty: He replaces 'good at coding' with the project bullet above and lists only skills he can demonstrate. Claiming a language he cannot use would be dishonest and could fail an interview.

Step 5, Statement of purpose: Limit 250 words: 40 words on the problem that interests him, 80 on why engineering, 80 on evidence from the lab project and courses, 50 on goals. 40 plus 80 plus 80 plus 50 is 250.

Step 6, Review: A teacher checks facts, he reads it aloud for flow, and he tracks hours weekly, aiming for 18 of 20. He keeps a second pathway in mind in case marks differ, because plans should be flexible.
Your turn: Plan 18 hours a week over 10 weeks for 3 science subjects. Model answer: for example 6 hours each; 18 times 10 is 180 hours; add timed past questions every second week and a rest day.

ladder: L1: kindness, honesty and sharing in daily life.
L2: responsibility, courage and care for others and nature.
L3: fairness, respect for difference and service.
L5: leadership, wellbeing and ethical reasoning.
L6 (degree): applied ethics, culture and community work.
L7 (postgraduate): scholarship, counselling or teaching at depth.
